# Week 7 Timed delivery

> [Download the Word version](W07_speed_trial_Speaker_Notes.docx) · This Markdown copy is generated from the DOCX. Update the DOCX, then run `python scripts/sync_documents.py --write` from the repository root. Print layout, page breaks, headers/footers, and writing-space height remain in Word.

Speaker notes for the one-hour timed delivery lesson using the two printed courses.

### Class preparation

**Print once**  Print W07\_speed\_trial\_Class\_Print\_Packet.pdf once on US Letter at Actual Size, single-sided, with automatic page orientation. Page 1 is the checklist, page 2 the assembly guide, pages 3–18 Kit A, 19–34 Kit B, 35–39 team sheets, 40–43 build cards and 44 attendance.

**Build both courses**  Trim the 16 tiles per course. Join rows A–H, L left of R when facing FINISH, using the paired ticks. Tape seams from behind and the courses flat. Verify the 5 cm ruler and measure exactly 60 cm between START on A and FINISH on D. Each 50 × 160 cm course has 90 cm of printed runout after FINISH. Leave clear floor at both ends.

**Set up both robots**  Load the complete W07\_speed\_trial.py on each kit. Check A left/B right, pair the correct hub, verify Stop and fit a loaded mentor tray. Put a narrow removable mark on the fixed side of each chassis where the timer can see it. Align that mark with START. Follow the slide 2 calibration steps on each kit and save the two baselines separately.

**Mentors and materials**  Assign two robot mentors and two build mentors. Use two stopwatches plus a rotation timer, two mentor trays, six lightweight cubes, four mounting proxies and four build packs. One mentor times all comparisons on their lane. If the lanes cannot be supervised independently, alternate and skip the optional speed block.

## Slide 1 Timed delivery challenge

**Timing**  0–5 minutes

**Open**  Ask which feature helped keep cargo in place in an earlier lesson. Today the teams deliver a cube through a timed 60 cm section, then test a removable cradle. Each child drives and explains one result.

**Success**  A valid delivery crosses the finish, keeps the cube aboard, stays in the lane and stops in the runout. A quick time is useful when the delivery succeeds reliably.

## Slide 2 Set up and calibrate both robots

**Timing**  5–10 minutes with slide 3. Complete the calibration before students arrive.

**Show the course**  Point to the START line, the 60 cm timed section and the 90 cm printed runout. Show the tape mark on the fixed chassis. Align it to START with the robot facing FINISH and a cube loaded. Check that the full robot has room at both ends.

**Calibrate Kit A and Kit B**  The supplied TRAVEL\_DEGREES = 0 prevents movement until configured. Set APPROVED\_SPEEDS = (200,) and start with TRAVEL\_DEGREES = 180 for a short test. Reset at the marked start, then increase in small steps up to the program limit of 1440 wheel degrees. Choose a setting that crosses FINISH and stops the whole loaded robot comfortably in the runout. Save that travel value on its own kit and keep it fixed when comparing runs.

**Approve loaded runs**  Pass three loaded runs at 200 on each kit. If time and stopping space allow, trial 300 and then optionally 400, keeping only speeds that pass three loaded runs. If only one kit passes, share that lane and skip higher speeds. If neither passes, hand-test the cradles, walk through the timing cues and record the runs as untested.

## Slide 3 When to start and stop the stopwatch

**Timing**  Within the 5–10 minute demonstration

**Show the start cue**  Stand beside the lane with a clear view of START and the FINISH line. The driver launches the program. R appears and the robot waits one second. Press START on the stopwatch when the chassis first moves. Have students say “start” as they see movement.

**Show the stop cue**  Point out the same tape mark on the chassis. Sight across the printed FINISH line and press STOP the instant that mark crosses it. A tray or bumper may extend farther forward. Use the same fixed mark and the same mentor timer for every comparison.

**Keep watching**  The robot continues into the runout after the timed crossing. D means the move ended. Record elapsed time to one decimal place, then judge cargo retention, lane position and where the robot fully stopped. Record DNF if the mark never crosses. Record the time and N if it crosses but fails another condition.

## Slide 4 Run three comparable trials

**Timing**  10–14 minutes for code and prediction. Rotate stations 14–26 and 26–38.

**Trace the code**  Use the full W07\_speed\_trial.py project. Students change the speed value passed to sprint(speed), using only an approved speed. A speed of 200 is measured in wheel degrees per second. The calibrated travel setting remains fixed.

**Robot station**  T1/T3 start on robots and T2/T4 at build tables, then swap. Rotate driver, navigator and observer every four minutes. Use the loaded mentor tray for A1–A3 at 200. If there is time and a higher setting passed rehearsal, use the same mentor tray and one approved speed for B1–B3. Mark B as skipped when needed.

**Build station**  Use the proxy to build and gently tilt a low removable cradle with rails and an end stop. Change one feature and compare. Rotate builder, designer and tester. A mentor checks fit and clearance before installing the cradle on the stopped robot.

## Slide 5 Compare the cradle at the same speed

**Timing**  38–44 minutes T1/T3, then 44–50 minutes T2/T4. Rotate jobs every two minutes.

**Retest**  Fit the approved team cradle. For C1–C3, choose the speed of a complete valid mentor-tray set. Keep that speed, travel value, cube, floor and start fixed so the cradle is the change. If there is no valid baseline, run a controlled 200 trial and record the limitation.

**Compare**  Count valid deliveries first. Only compare mean times for complete 3/3 valid sets from the same kit and timing method. Keep failed attempts visible. As a calculation example, 3.0, 3.2 and 3.1 seconds average 3.1 seconds. Close stopwatch results can count as a tie.

## Slide 6 Save the evidence for the showcase

**Timing**  50–54 minutes for reflection and 54–60 minutes for saving and packing.

**Ask**  Give each child a short turn to explain a speed choice, a cradle change, or one observed result. Ask which configuration completed three valid runs and why the team would choose it.

**Save**  Save each team’s tested project with kit ID, calibrated travel value, approved speed and chosen tray. Keep trial sheets private, label each cradle and stop and charge the hubs. Log actual rehearsal and class results.

**Week 8**  Use the saved timed delivery project and the same course and timing rules. Choose a configuration that passed 3/3. Keep the existing four-minute showcase slots. If a run fails, explain the observed result and show the earlier trial evidence.

**Technical source**  The paired finite-movement pattern follows LEGO Education Make It Move: https://education.lego.com/en-au/lessons/spike-python-u9-data-and-math-functions/spike-python-u9l4-make-it-move/. The course dimensions and timing rules are classroom choices.
